I’ll go back and check it, sometimes three or four times, even when I remember turning the knob. Same at home with the front door and the stove—my wife says she saw me lock it, but I still have to jiggle it a few times and sometimes go back again after we’re in bed.

Lately I’ve started getting this idea that something in the air, or on people’s hands, is “wrong” or dangerous in a way I can’t explain. I wash my hands over and over during service, more than what’s needed for hygiene. If I touch the trash or a delivery box, I feel almost contaminated, like something could get inside me or my food, and I scrub until my skin gets red.

I know some of these fears might not be reasonable, but they feel very convincing in the moment, like I’d be irresponsible or put people at risk if I didn’t follow them.

At work, I can’t stop thinking that the gas burners are still on or that I’ve left a knife in a dangerous place, even after I’ve checked them. I’ll turn the knobs off, step away, and then this thought hits me that something bad will happen if I don’t recheck. I end up going back again and again, sometimes ten or fifteen times, until my prep is behind and my staff are annoyed.  

I’ve also become convinced that if there’s even a tiny bit of raw chicken juice on my hands or the counter, my wife or customers could get seriously sick and it would be my fault. I know it sounds over the top, but in the moment it feels absolutely true and terrifying. So I wash my hands constantly—like every few minutes during service—and scrub the counters at home over and over. My hands are cracked from all the soap.  

I don’t hear voices, don’t see things, and I know these thoughts are coming from me, but I just can’t shake them or stop the rituals.
